title: Noom Med vs FutureClinic: GLP-1 programs, or a doctor by message
summary: Noom GLP-1 vs FutureClinic compares Noom Med's plans and prices with a $40 FutureClinic visit where a doctor reads your case and answers by message.
body_markdown:
Noom Med combines its behavior-change app, AI food logging, and compounded microdose or brand GLP-1 plans into a recurring monthly[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) , filling compounded prescriptions through its partner pharmacies. FutureClinic separates the doctor visit from the pharmacy: you pay $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100, with no subscription required, for convenient digital care without tying your prescription to a single pharmacy.


At FutureClinic, no form gets approved in bulk. A specific doctor reads your whole case and answers you with a Human Signature: a short live video or voice note recorded for you. Every clinician is a physician with an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a[nurse practitioner](https://futureclinic.com/blog/nurse-practitioner-vs-doctor-who-treats-you-online) or a physician assistant. Whenever you return, weeks or months later, you message that same doctor in the same chat to build trust, try treatments together, and track progress.


For[weight loss](https://futureclinic.com/blog/weight-loss-medication-online-no-membership-fee) , staying with the same doctor over months means adjusting a GLP-1 dose, swapping a medicine that irritates you, reading new labs against last year's, and deciding together when to step up or hold steady. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, never upselling a medicine or lab panel. You never stay subscribed to keep your medicine, and if your doctor decides it's right for you, they can prescribe any fitting brand or generic medicine to the pharmacy you choose, with no house formulary.


## How does a weight-loss program compare with a doctor by message?


Noom Med treats a fixed menu. As of October 2026, Noom states that "Members work with licensed clinicians who prescribe and manage medications," including "Experienced telehealth and obesity physicians" via outside clinical partners. Nurse practitioner use and keeping the same clinician are not stated. Alongside weight loss, Noom lists "Menopause & HRT"; unrelated care is not stated.


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. Generalists and specialists practice across more than 60 specialties. Your doctor can help with other problems in their specialty: an internal medicine or family doctor managing weight can also treat blood pressure, and a dermatologist treating hair loss can treat acne or eczema. Every FutureClinic doctor you see works from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


Would you rather have Noom's weight-loss program, food-logging app, and monthly medication plan, or a physician who manages your care by message? If you want the app and bundled plan Noom builds around the clinician, Noom Med is a strong option, and if you wanted an expert doctor with nothing else attached, FutureClinic gives you that.


We believe AI is a tool for doctors, with the human doctor in charge of every case. Health problems have nuance requiring one-to-one human attention, and only an expert knows when an AI makes a mistake or heads toward the wrong answer. On FutureClinic, the AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident, gathering your history and preparing a summary you confirm before the doctor sees it, and it never gives medical advice by itself. Real care from a doctor takes hours, not seconds: replies typically come within a few hours, and almost always the same day or the next.

Noom FutureClinic

**What you pay** Microdose from $79 plus tax, then $179/month plus tax (medicine included); dual-pathway $149, then $299/month; brand from $39 plus medicine; Medicare Bridge $39 start, $387/12 weeks, $50/fill (as of October 2026) $40 for best-fit doctor, or chosen doctor's price, typically $20 to $100; optional membership, typically $25 to $100/month

## What do Noom Med and FutureClinic cost over a year?


As of October 2026, Noom's compounded microdose semaglutide and tirzepatide plan costs "from $79 plus tax and $179 per month plus tax" with medicine included ($2,048 before tax over a year), and its dual-pathway GLP-1 plan is $149 plus tax for 4 weeks, then $299 a month plus tax. Because those compounded medicines come only from Noom's partner pharmacies, you stay subscribed to keep getting refills. Brand plans start at $39 plus the medicine, and Noom's Medicare GLP-1 Bridge is $39 to start and $387 every 12 weeks ($1,587 a year) plus $50 per fill.


With FutureClinic, a visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100, and most doctors offer an optional membership (typically $25 to $100 a month) for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time. For a stable medicine, one visit can cover several months when your doctor judges it safe, if your doctor decides it's right for you, sent to the pharmacy you choose (local pickup, mail-order home delivery, LillyDirect, or NovoCare) with a cash discount coupon, and FutureClinic helps with prior authorizations. With commercial insurance, maker savings cards lower Wegovy to as little as $25 a month (up to $100 a month in savings, as of October 2026), and eligible Part D members pay $50 a month for Wegovy, Zepbound KwikPen, or Foundayo under the federal Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027). Paying cash (as of October 2026), NovoCare and TrumpRx retail coupons price the 1.5 mg Wegovy pill at $149 a month ($1,788 for a year at that dose, plus a $40 visit; $199 a month at 4 mg and $299 at 9 and 25 mg), while the Wegovy pen is $199 a month for the first two fills for new patients on 0.25 mg and 0.5 mg through December 31, 2026, then $349. At LillyDirect (as of October 2026), self-pay starts at $149 a month for the 0.8 mg Foundayo pill and $299 a month for 2.5 mg Zepbound (KwikPen or vial).
